AFLAX Alumni
Connections

Forging Falcons, on and off the field

One members-only portal that keeps the Air Force Lacrosse brotherhood connected after graduation, and gives cadets an AI mentor that introduces them to alumni who have lived the job.

Mitch Rose | USAFA ’17 · AFLAX Alumni Board, Cadet Mentorship
01

The problem & who has it

Alumni

The brotherhood fades after graduation

~850+AFLAX alumni since 1967 (est. ~15 per class)
~25show up to Fall Alumni Weekend each year (≈3%)
  • The only links today: an email list and a basic website
  • Nobody knows who is at which base, doing which job
  • The team’s travel, food, and quality of life depend on alumni donations

Cadets

Life-shaping choices made blind

  • Every cadet picks an AFSC: the job they will do for the rest of their career
  • The prep: PowerPoints and rare guest speakers
  • Then they rank base preferences with almost no knowledge of each base
  • No mentorship program exists, so cadets rely mostly on other cadets’ opinions
Who has it: ~15 graduating AFLAX cadets a year, every alum who has lost touch, and an alumni board with no tools to connect them.

What’s new about our solution

Today
AFLAX Alumni Connections
Email list + public website
➜
Members-only portal: every account approved by the alumni board
“Who’s where?” lives in people’s heads
➜
Live world map of alumni, filtered by status, base, and AFSC, plus a contact roster
Schedule on the athletics site
➜
Schedule + venue map + tailgates, with RSVPs, calendar invites, and miles from you
Career advice from other cadets
➜
Falcon Mentor: an AI agent grounded in official AFSC data and an 81-base guide
Chatbots that only talk
➜
An agent that connects: recommends real, opted-in alumni and drafts the intro email
The key idea: the AI’s job isn’t to be the mentor. It’s to introduce the cadet to the right human mentor, and it can only recommend people who actually exist in the database.
03

How the agent works

Member

Cadet or alum asks: “Who can I talk to about Wright-Patterson?”

Portal + API

React site → FastAPI: login check, rate limit, last 6 messages + running memo

Falcon Mentor

PydanticAI agent · gpt-6-luna via Portkey (Responses API) · decides which tools to call

Answer

Structured reply + mentor cards built from the database + optional intro email
▼ the agent calls tools ▼                      ▲ results checked before replying ▲
Career fieldssearch_afscs · get_afsc_detailsOfficial AFSC PDF + plain-language guide (36 AFSCs)
Basessearch_bases · get_base_detailsCurated guide: 81 bases, missions, aircraft, pros & cons
Alumnifind_mentors · count_alumniMember database: only approved, opted-in alumni
Outreachdraft_intro_messagePolite first email, signed with the cadet’s name & class
  1. The question arrives with who’s asking (class, status) and the memo of earlier topics
  2. The agent plans and calls only the tools it needs (often in parallel)
  3. Tools return facts from real data, never from the model’s memory
  4. Output validator: every recommended mentor must be a real, approved, opted-in alum, or the agent must retry
  5. Emails and phones come from the database, not the AI; the memo and token usage are saved

Cost to run

Measured across 8 real Falcon Mentor questions

$0.0009 per message

≈ $0.90 per 1,000 messages

Model calls / tool calls (average)2.9 / 4.3
Input tokens (76% served from prompt cache)6,905
Output tokens420
gpt-6-luna on Azure, per 1M tokens$0.10 in · $0.50 out

Cached input is priced at the full input rate here, so these figures run high. The Board usage panel tracks real cost as members use it.

What that means

100 members × 20 questions a month≈ $1.80 / mo
Every alum (~850) asks 5 questions in a year≈ $3.80 / yr
Worst case: 100 members max out the 40/day cap every day≈ $108 / mo max

Everything else is free and open-source: React, FastAPI, SQLite, OpenStreetMap maps. No paid APIs beyond the model (hosting not included).

How we kept it cheap

Prompt caching (76% hit)Trimmed tool results6-message history + memo Explorer answers for $0Low reasoning effort6/min · 40/day capsUsage dashboard
07

Safety measures

🛡️Board-approved access

  • Every account is reviewed by the alumni board
  • Approval is rechecked on every request, so revoking access is instant
  • Only board members can edit the schedule

🔐Account security

  • Salted, hashed passwords (PBKDF2)
  • Server-side sessions; logout and password changes end other logins
  • Lockout after 5 failed logins; single-use 1-hour reset links

🤖AI guardrails

  • Validator blocks invented mentors
  • Contact info comes from the database, never the model
  • Prompt-injection defense: member text is treated as data, with length limits
  • Stays on topic; tells cadets to confirm official details with their AOC/AFPC

👤Privacy

  • Photos re-encoded: GPS and metadata stripped, real-image check
  • Photos only served through signed, expiring links
  • Members can hide their phone number; test data is fictional

💸Cost guardrails

  • Per-member limits: 6 messages a minute, 40 a day
  • Hard cap per answer: 8 model calls, 60k tokens
  • Board dashboard shows usage, cache hits, and cost

✅Hardening & testing

  • Security headers; HTTPS + HSTS ready
  • Versioned database migrations
  • 30 automated tests, including a full offline chat run

Impact: the numbers

~3%of an estimated 850+ alumni attend Fall Alumni Weekend (~25 a year). The gap this portal is built to close.
59years of Air Force Lacrosse history (since 1967) to reconnect
~15cadets graduate each year and face the AFSC + base decision
52men on today’s roster: the alumni network is ~16× larger
36officer AFSCs explained in plain language, linked to alumni who hold them
81Air & Space Force bases with missions, aircraft, and honest pros & cons
7agent tools that turn a question into a real introduction
<$0.001per Falcon Mentor message; 100 active members for a year ≈ $22
